source_excerpts.text:
(B) For every finite reference, faithful baseline sigma, and Hermitian H with H_R=0,

    g^S_(P sigma)(P H) <= c g^S_(Q sigma)(Q H).

Outputs are restricted to their effective support when necessary. The statement extends to boundary pairs whose displayed relative entropies are finite by the usual common faithful regularization.

Taking Q to be the identity proves that the conditional Umegaki contraction coefficient equals the complete equal-reference SLD metric coefficient for every quantum channel. It does NOT identify either with the complete equal-reference Umegaki coefficient.

source.quote: Its reference marginal is independent of epsilon:
source.range_scope: Receiving necessity construction and unequal reference marginals.

source_excerpts.text:
For sufficiently small epsilon of either sign, beta(epsilon) is faithful. Its trace is one because Tr L=0. Its reference marginal is independent of epsilon:

    alpha_RC=sigma_R tensor tau,
    beta(epsilon)_RC=sigma_R tensor W/Z.

At epsilon=0, every output channel has joint relative entropy D(tau||W/Z), equal to the reference relative entropy. Therefore its conditional relative-entropy deficit is exactly zero at the baseline. Auxiliary conjugation diag(-1,1,...,1) sends epsilon to -epsilon while leaving alpha fixed, so each deficit is even.

source.quote: Since both conditional baselines vanish, (A) implies B_P<=c B_Q.

source_excerpts.text: Since both conditional baselines vanish, (A) implies B_P<=c B_Q. This is valid for every finite c. One cannot instead differentiate a raw-relative-entropy comparison with arbitrary c at the same construction: its nonzero common baseline would not cancel unless c=1.

statement: For finite-dimensional quantum channels P,Q with common input, uniform conditional Umegaki order is equivalent to complete equal-reference SLD metric order with the same constant, for arbitrary finite references. The necessity construction is a conditional-order argument with H_R=0 and deliberately different reference marginals. The coherent-qubit SLD-to-BKM integral is prior work by Hirche, Proposition 3.5 / Eq. (3.18); the conditional reference-score gauge and reverse finite-filter construction are separate receiving steps.
title: Conditional Umegaki and complete equal-reference SLD order share a constant
